steps.title: Fit the model
steps.description: Estimate the odds ratio of a red card per game.

options.label: Binomial GLM
options.rationale: Red cards out of games is a binomial outcome.
options.spec: GLM Binomial on (redCards, games - redCards); OR = exp(coef).
options.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    covariates = list(ctx.get("covariates", []))
    needed = ["skin_tone", "games", "redCards", "playerShort"] + covariates
    data = df.dropna(subset=needed).copy()
    data["playerShort"] = data["playerShort"].astype(str)
    numeric = [c for c in covariates if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    categorical = [c for c in covariates if c not in numeric]
    parts = [data[["skin_tone"]].astype(float), data[numeric].astype(float)]
    if categorical:
        parts.append(
            pd.get_dummies(data[categorical].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        )
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant="add")
    successes = data["redCards"].clip(upper=data["games"]).astype(float)
    endog = pd.concat([successes, data["games"].astype(float) - successes], axis=1)
    fit = sm.GLM(endog, exog, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit()
    low, high = fit.conf_int().loc["skin_tone"]
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(fit.params["skin_tone"])),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": float(fit.pvalues["skin_tone"]),
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "extra": {"log_odds": float(fit.params["skin_tone"])},
    }

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    covariates = list(ctx.get("covariates", []))
    needed = ["skin_tone", "games", "redCards", "playerShort"] + covariates
    data = df.dropna(subset=needed).copy()
    data["playerShort"] = data["playerShort"].astype(str)
    numeric = [c for c in covariates if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    categorical = [c for c in covariates if c not in numeric]
    parts = [data[["skin_tone"]].astype(float), data[numeric].astype(float)]
    if categorical:
        parts.append(
            pd.get_dummies(data[categorical].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        )
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant="add")
    successes = data["redCards"].clip(upper=data["games"]).astype(float)
    endog = pd.concat([successes, data["games"].astype(float) - successes], axis=1)
    groups = pd.factorize(data["playerShort"])[0]
    fit = sm.GLM(endog, exog, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit(
        cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": groups}
    )
    low, high = fit.conf_int().loc["skin_tone"]
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(fit.params["skin_tone"])),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": float(fit.pvalues["skin_tone"]),
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "extra": {"log_odds": float(fit.params["skin_tone"])},
    }

option.label: Only referees from low implicit-bias countries
option.rationale: Cleaner comparison among referees with less measured bias.

data.reason: Adjusting for referee-country bias scores is a standard confounder control, keeps the population and the estimand unchanged, and was used by published analysts.
Keeping only low-bias referees changes the population and tests the question where bias is least likely, so a null there says nothing about referees in general.

report.narrative: With the default choices dark-skinned players are carded more: OR 1.34 (95% CI 1.13 to 1.58), p = 0.0006, n = 124,621 dyads, so the verdict is BIAS DETECTED. None of the 9 single-decision changes reverses it: the odds ratio stays between 1.27 and 1.36 and every interval keeps excluding 1. None of the 10 pairs ranked most likely to flip it does either. The verdict first changes at three simultaneous changes: 4 such universes reach NO CLEAR EVIDENCE, with odds ratios of 1.20 to 1.25 and p between 0.055 and 0.069. All of them adjust for the full covariate set, and most add player-clustered errors and the second rater alone. The minimal flip (second rater only, referees with 22 or more dyads, full covariates; OR 1.20 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.46), p = 0.055) was re-executed from a fresh sandbox and reproduced exactly. Across all defensible universes the odds ratio runs from 1.20 to 1.36, inside the human teams' range of 0.89 to 2.93. The only one-decision change that did flip the verdict, keeping low-bias referees only (OR 1.25 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.59), p = 0.066), was rejected as an indefensible change of population.
caveats: Odds ratios compare the lightest with the darkest tone on a 0 to 1 scale and rest on player-referee dyads, not on individual refereeing decisions.
The estimate is an association; it cannot separate bias from unmeasured differences in playing style or match context.
Influence is measured under fixed defaults and is not a causal statement about the world.
